title: Understanding and Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models for Tabular Data
summary: Gives the first systematic study of memorization in tabular diffusion models, showing that near-identical training rows are replicated more as training lengthens and as the dataset shrinks, and proposes TabCutMix and TabCutMixPlus, which swap feature subsets between same-class training rows, the Plus variant restricting swaps to correlation-clustered features, to cut replication without losing sample quality. The evaluation is run on SDMetrics: the shape and trend scores are its KSComplement and TVComplement metrics and the machine learning efficacy metrics are taken from the same package, while CTGAN and TVAE are two of the generators the mitigation is shown to carry over to.
evidence: Appendix D.4.1 states the shape score of numerical and categorical features is determined by the KSComplement and TVComplement metrics in the SDMetrics package, with footnote 16 giving https://docs.sdv.dev/sdmetrics; appendix D.4.2 states the implementations of the evaluation metrics are sourced from SDMetrics and that the paper follows their guidelines for consistency across real and synthetic data assessments, footnoted to the same URL; appendix D.2 describes CTGAN and TVAE as baseline methods employed in the study, crediting CTGAN with mode-specific normalization and conditional generation and TVAE with the same encoding under a VAE framework; appendix E.8 Table 9 reports memorization ratio, MLE, alpha-precision, beta-recall, shape score, trend score, C2ST and DCR for CTGAN and TVAE with and without TabCutMixPlus on Default, Adult, Shoppers and Magic

title: TabGen-ICL: Residual-Aware In-Context Example Selection for Tabular Data Generation
summary: Generates tabular data by prompting a fixed large language model rather than fine-tuning one, selecting in-context examples that cover the residual between the real distribution and what has been generated so far, so each round of prompting corrects the gap the previous round left. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN-based and VAE-based entries among the deep generative baselines it is measured against on marginal, correlation, precision, recall, C2ST and Jensen-Shannon divergence.
evidence: Section 2 describes CTGAN and TVAE, both cited to Xu et al. 2019, as dealing with mixed-type tabular data generation under the GAN and VAE frameworks; section 5 lists the deep generative baselines as the VAE-based method TVAE, the GAN-based method CTGAN, four diffusion methods and two autoregressive methods, alongside LLM-based methods with and without fine-tuning; the results table reports TVAE and CTGAN rows on marginal, correlation, precision, recall, C2ST and JSD against TABGEN-ICL

title: Debt Collection Negotiations with Large Language Models: An Evaluation System and Optimizing Decision Making with Multi-Agent
summary: Builds an evaluation system for debt collection negotiation that scores an agent on both the negotiation process and its outcome, and proposes a multi-agent framework with planning and judging modules tuned by direct preference optimization with reject sampling. CTGAN produces the benchmark itself: the 975-record debt dataset is synthesized from real records held by a financial technology company in order to meet privacy compliance, then sampled to match the original distribution by gender, overdue days and loan amount, so every result in the paper is measured on CTGAN output.
evidence: The introduction states that to ensure both privacy and data validity CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, was used to generate synthetic data based on debt records from a leading financial technology company, and that a dataset of 975 debt records was constructed; section 2.1 repeats that CTGAN was used to generate synthetic data for privacy compliance and that the data was categorized by gender, overdue days and loan amount then sampled to match the distribution patterns of the original data; the conclusion states that by leveraging synthetic debt data generated through CTGAN the paper evaluated various AI-driven strategies

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Synthetic Tabular Data Generation
summary: Surveys synthetic tabular data generation under a three-fold taxonomy of traditional machine learning methods, diffusion models and large language model approaches, comparing them on data type compatibility, fidelity, privacy resilience and downstream performance, and cataloguing the datasets and metrics the field uses. CTGAN is one of the surveyed methods rather than a tool the survey runs: it heads the conditional GAN branch of the taxonomy with TVAE under the VAE branch, and the prose credits it with the PacGAN discriminator, a combined generator and gradient-penalty Wasserstein loss, and training-by-sampling for imbalanced categorical features.
evidence: Figure 3 and Table I place CTGAN, cited as 2019 NeurIPS, in the conditional GAN branch of the GAN-based methods alongside cGANs, CTAB-GAN, OCT-GAN, cWGAN and RC-TGAN, with TVAE in the VAE-based branch; section III-A states CTGAN enhances cGANs by incorporating the PacGAN structure in the discriminator and employing a combination of generator loss, Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty and a training-by-sampling strategy to handle imbalanced categorical features, and a later section names cGAN, CTAB-GAN and CTGAN as the models that incorporate conditional vectors to synthesize minority-class samples; the survey reports comparative numbers in tables but describes its own contribution as a side-by-side comparison across paradigms rather than a new experimental study, so CTGAN is recorded as described and not run

title: A Conditional GAN for Tabular Data Generation with Probabilistic Sampling of Latent Subspaces
summary: Proposes ctdGAN, a conditional tabular GAN that first clusters the training rows, then samples the latent space in proportion to cluster and class probabilities, conditioning the generator on both the class label and the cluster so that minority regions are reached without a separate oversampling step. It builds on CTGAN in two places, taking its dual generator output of a hyperbolic tangent for continuous values and a Gumbel softmax for discrete ones and the first two terms of its generator loss, while replacing CTGAN's variational Gaussian mixture normalization with a cluster-based scheme on the grounds that the mixture inflates dimensionality; CTGAN and TVAE are also among the compared generators.
evidence: Section 3 states that for the generator output ctdGAN adopts the strategy of ctGAN, generating continuous values by a hyperbolic tangent and discrete ones by Gumbel softmax; the loss section states the first two terms of Equation 10 are also used by ctGAN and CTAB-GAN and adds two class and cluster terms of its own; section 2 states ctGAN employs a Variational Gaussian Mixture Model to normalize continuous columns and capture multiple modes, that its high dimensional output hurts training time, and that ctdGAN instead uses a simple cluster-based normalization; CTGAN, TVAE and CTAB-GAN appear as compared generators in the experiments. The paper spells the model ctGAN throughout

title: Limited Reference, Reliable Generation: A Two-Component Framework for Tabular Data Generation in Low-Data Regimes
summary: Targets tabular generation when only tens of reference rows exist, pairing a component that distils decision-tree logic into compact rules to guide a language model with a dual-granularity filter that screens generated rows at both the instance and the chunk level, and reports gains over both deep generative and prompt-based baselines at sample sizes from 30 to 500. CTGAN reaches the paper twice: it is named in related work as the classical method the paper departs from, faulted for mode collapse and heavy preprocessing, and it is the generator underneath the DRL constraint baseline, which the hyper-parameter table labels CTGAN-based and trains for 150 epochs at batch size 24.
evidence: Section 2.1 states CTGAN, cited to Xu et al. 2019, extends GANs to handle mixed-type variables but suffers from mode collapse and requires heavy preprocessing; the experimental setup lists DRL, the Disjunctive Refinement Layers generator of Stoian and Giunchiglia 2025, as the constraint-based baseline and notes it builds on a GAN-based formulation; Table 5 gives the hyper-parameters for the non-LLM baselines and labels the row DRL (CTGAN-based) with 150 epochs, batch size 24 and Adam at 2e-4; DRL columns appear in every results table. The downloaded PDF carries the later title Rule-Guided Tabular Data Generation with Dual-Granularity Filtering; the title recorded here is the one the DOI record and citation pool carry
needs: Convention question, related to the open question on paper-constrained-dgm-realistic-2024. The rule that benchmarking a CTGAN descendant is citation_only was written for standalone descendant models such as CTAB-GAN+. Here the baseline is a constraint layer wrapped around CTGAN itself, trained with CTGAN's own hyper-parameters, so CTGAN is the generator actually run. Recorded baseline_only 3 on that reading; citation_only 2 is the alternative

title: Improving Cardiac Risk Prediction Using Data Generation Techniques
summary: Models cardiac rehabilitation as a business process and addresses the small, imbalanced patient records it yields by proposing conditional variational autoencoder variants with supervised and contrastive latent structure, then measuring whether classifiers trained on the augmented sets predict risk better than those trained on the original data. CTGAN is one of three publicly available generators run as the state-of-the-art comparison, with hyper-parameters from its original publication, and the paper reports it failing on this dataset: it achieves low accuracy for the at-risk class and shifts the original distribution despite being conditional.
evidence: The experimental section states the proposed architectures are compared with three state-of-the-art generative models with publicly available implementations, CTGAN, TTVAE and WGAN-GP, with hyper-parameters following the settings of the original publications; the discussion states that CTGAN, TTVAE and WGAN-GP perform noticeably below the VAE-based variants and never rank among the best-performing sets, and that CTGAN, although conditional, achieves low accuracy for the at-risk class and alters the original distribution; Table 2 reports CTGAN at doubled and quintupled synthetic set sizes against the proposed CVAE variants. Reference [21] resolves to Xu, Skoularidou, Cuesta-Infante and Veeramachaneni. TTVAE here is the transformer-based model of Wang and Nguyen, not SDV's TVAE
